judgments.reasoning_cat1: One sentence of boilerplate corporate authority; no term with competing meanings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Mirrored exactly by X.B.3 for the University; no tension anywhere else.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional no-litigation representation qualified by "best knowledge"; the last sentence largely repeats the first, which is redundant rather than ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Mirrors X.B.4 (which adds an adverse-impact qualifier) without contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[R]easonable assurance of the funding necessary" is a vague, almost unenforceable standard — no financial statements, covenants or thresholds — and the clause misspells the party as "EENET".
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing else in the instrument addresses ENET's finances, though XI.B(3) lets ENET walk away if it ceases wireless cable service, which dilutes the assurance.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Plain organisation and eligibility representation; the added FCC-eligibility element is specific.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with VIII.A's licence-maintenance duty and X.A.1's mirror.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[I]n all material respects" is a familiar qualifier and the rest is standard no-conflict language.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Hybrid Agreement is a commitment to which the University is bound, and XIII.Q acknowledges potential conflicts between the two agreements, which sits uneasily with the representation of no conflict with any agreement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Boilerplate authority representation; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Mirrors X.A.3; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Conventional no-litigation representation with knowledge and adverse-impact qualifiers.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Parallel to X.A.4; no conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A flat accuracy warranty about Schedule B; its only softness is that Schedule B as annexed contains entries marked "Omitted" and incomplete coordinates.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: III.B requires ENET to reorient antennas at receive sites "listed on Schedule A", contradicting this clause's identification of Schedule B as the receive-site schedule.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Survival and continuing-representation language in ordinary terms; "might reasonably be deemed to constitute a breach of or lead to a breach" is loose but ancillary.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It converts one-time representations into continuing ones, which meshes with the covenant-style wording already in X.A and X.B; no conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Limb (2)(b) is garbled — "(if the breach ts other than for the payment of money) ENET has not undertaken material or substantive measures to cure" — and "material obligations" and "material or substantive measures" are undefined and overlapping, so the cure standard is genuinely uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It terminates "without further liability to ENET" while XI.C preserves the terminating party's damages claims, and III.A gives the University a $1.00 equipment purchase right only on a XI.A termination — so which route was taken matters.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Limb (3) lets ENET terminate simply "if ENET ceases to provide wireless cable service" — an event wholly within ENET's control, with no notice period — and limb (1)'s exception refers to a breach "by ENET" in a clause about the University's FCC authority.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: A unilateral exit at ENET's option is hard to reconcile with the fixed initial term in I.A, the automatic renewal in I.B and the ninety-day non-renewal notice, and with XI.C's preservation of damages; III.A's carve-out for "the exercise by ENET of its rights under Section XI.B.(2)" also mis-describes this clause.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Short and apparently plain, but it preserves damages only for "the terminating party", saying nothing about the party terminated against.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: XI.A and XI.B each confer the right to terminate "without further liability" to the other party, and II.D.1, II.D.2, II.E.1 and II.E.2 terminate "without further liability between the parties" — XI.C's preservation of damages pulls directly against that language.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The first sentence is syntactically broken: the qualifier "subject to the approval of the University, which approval shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned or delayed" is spliced into the middle of the filing obligation, and the second sentence then gives the University an unqualified veto "[n]otwithstanding anything herein to the contrary".
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The absolute consent right conflicts with the reasonableness qualifier in the same clause and with II.A.2/II.C.1, which require the University to file or amend applications at ENET's request on a best-efforts basis, and with III.E.3's protection of ENET's siting interest.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause uses "best reasonable efforts" and "reasonable best efforts" in consecutive sentences, and "any additional facilities which ENET may desire in order to optimize its business within the Washington/Baltimore area" is open-ended (and geographically wider than the rest of the Agreement).
judgments.reasoning_cat2: VIII.A imposes a "best efforts"/"all necessary steps" licence-maintenance duty over the same ground, and the Washington/Baltimore reference exceeds the "Washington, DC metropolitan area" used in the recitals and XI.B(3).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "In addition to any other obligations" plus "all reasonable costs and expenses" is broad, and "incurred by the University" appears twice, but the meaning is discernible.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: XIII.N opens "[n]otwithstanding anything to the contrary contained herein" and caps negotiating legal and engineering fees at $15,000, while this clause and II.F promise uncapped reimbursement — a genuine allocation conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause first allows assignment only if the assignee assumes all obligations and then, "[s]ubject to the foregoing provisions", allows assignment to "an entity that does not agree to assume all remaining obligations" — an internal contradiction on the face of the paragraph.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It duplicates VIII.B's assignment machinery almost verbatim but with different triggers, and its fee-sharing sentence says ENET "shall notify" where the parallel sentence in II.B says ENET "may notify".

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard counterparts clause; nothing contestable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the execution block and XIII.D; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "ENET shall assist in the development of such program" states an obligation with no content, standard or limit, and "sufficiently in advance" is similarly unbounded.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It rests on a statement of the University's "intention", which reads more like a recital than an operative term, and it presupposes University Capacity as allocated by IV; no direct conflict, though the distance-learning use overlaps the recapture windows.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional integration and written-modification clause; "with respect to the subject matter" is the only soft boundary.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Agreement expressly preserves and subordinates itself to the Hybrid Agreement in XIII.Q and relies on it in II.C.1 and III.E.1, so the sweep of the integration clause has to be read against those provisions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bare acknowledgement of executory character with no operative content.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It states nothing that could contradict another clause, though its evident bankruptcy-facing purpose is not developed anywhere else.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A list of specific events closing with "or other contingencies beyond the reasonable control of the parties" invites an ejusdem generis argument, and "the period of dependency of any such contingency" appears to be a mechanical error for "pendency".
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It begins "[n]otwithstanding anything contained in this Agreement to the contrary" and suspends payments, which sits against XIII.R's time-of-the-essence clause and V.B's monthly royalty floor.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[W]ill not take any action which would adversely affect the rights granted by it to the other party" is an extremely broad negative covenant with no qualification.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read literally it would bar the University from exercising VIII.B (returning or not renewing the licence) and XIII.A (assigning to a non-assuming entity), both of which the Agreement expressly permits.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Choosing federal communications law, FCC rules and DC law together leaves the hierarchy among them unstated, but the intent is discernible.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It works with XIII.K's DC forum selection; no contrary provision.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Ordinary headings clause; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The instrument's headings are OCR-garbled in places, so disclaiming them is if anything helpful; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It disclaims contra proferentem in clear terms; the only oddity is that it presupposes the Agreement may "require interpretation or construction".
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It bears on how the one-sided clauses elsewhere (VII, XII.A, XIII.N) would be read, but does not conflict with any of them.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[A]ny party shall have the right to sue the other party in District of Columbia courts" is permissive in form yet followed by irrevocable submission and waiver of all objections, leaving it unclear whether the forum is exclusive.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cross-refers to the Notices section for service, which is consistent with XIII.L; no other conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[D]eemed given the first weekday ... after being sent" fixes effectiveness on dispatch rather than receipt while simultaneously requiring return receipt or signature — a small internal friction — and it permits only two delivery methods.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The carve-out "[e]xcept as set forth above concerning the payment of Royalties" matches V.C's first-class-mail rule, and the many notice deadlines in I.C, II.D, II.E and XI depend on this deemed-delivery rule.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "ENET shall have the exclusive tight to lease the capacity of channel D2 for the duration of this Agreement" is drafted as both an exclusive right and an option with a 21-day exercise window, and the added royalty ("greater of $2,500 or $.10 per subscriber") repeats the missing-enumerator problem of V.B.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It presupposes ENET can take D2 capacity, which collides with XIII.Q's subordination of ENET's rights to the Hybrid Agreement and with IV, which allocates only D3 and D4 as ENET Capacity and deems all other capacity University Capacity.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The $15,000 cap is placed in a parenthesis that may attach only to negotiating fees, leaving the following items (operating and maintaining the station, "otherwise complying with the terms of this Agreement") uncapped and very broad.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It opens "[n]otwithstanding anything to the contrary contained herein" yet II.F and XII.C promise reimbursement of all reasonable costs without a cap, and III.D makes ENET bear operating costs directly rather than by reimbursement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[A]n airtime use relationship and not a joint venture" is a standard characterisation clause; the second sentence's "nor as having any relationship with one another" is oddly absolute but qualified by the carve-out.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: XIII.C requires ENET to list the University's programming in its guide and III.A/III.D contemplate joint operations, which is a mild tension with the no-relationship language.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An agreement to "promptly negotiate in good faith to reform and amend" with no fallback, plus a prohibition on any action that "contributes to" an adverse regulatory change — a standard of causation that is very hard to apply.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overlaps with XIII.P.2's acknowledgement that capacity allocation is subject to FCC rule changes and with II.A.2's negotiate-or-terminate mechanism, without saying which prevails.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bare acknowledgement with no operative effect; its only defect is citing the Report and Order as released "July 9, 1994".
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section IV cites the same Report and Order, MM Docket No. 93-106, as released "July 6, 1994", and the acknowledgement that capacity allocation may change undercuts IV's fixed D3/D4 allocation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The obligation to "be read to conform" to unspecified Hybrid Agreement duties imports an undisclosed document, and "no action shall be taken hereunder" that in the University's "reasonable judgment" would adversely affect Hybrid is a very wide veto.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Despite its "[n]otwithstanding anything to the contrary" opening, it is hard to reconcile with XIII.M's exclusive option over channel D2 and with IV's deeming of non-ENET capacity as University Capacity.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One sentence, definite in terms; time of the essence for every stated period.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is in tension with XIII.F's force majeure extension of "all requirements as to notice and other performance" and with the soft deadlines elsewhere ("as soon as reasonably possible" in III.A, "promptly" in II.A.2).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The sentence is convoluted and the phrase "or of any other failure in the future or in the past" is awkward, but the non-waiver intent is plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It supports the cure and termination machinery in XI without contradicting it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard interpretive rules and a conventional two-limb "Final Order" definition; "[a]ll pronouns and any variations therefore" is a spelling slip that does not change meaning.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Final Order definition is invoked repeatedly in II.D, II.E, III.A, VIII.B and XIII.A and is consistent with those uses; II.D.1's cross-reference to "Paragraph XIII.T" is accurate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The schedule describes itself as listing merely "representative types of programming that Eastern intends to transmit" — an intention, not a permission — and it cites "Subparagraph 3 (C)", a provision that does not exist in this Agreement, while naming "Eastern" rather than the defined ENET.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section VII treats Schedule A as the operative list of programming networks ENET "may utilize ENET Capacity to transmit", which is inconsistent with the schedule's own self-description as merely representative, and III.B wrongly cites Schedule A for receive sites.
